$comment: Fixed Miro layout for the Opportunity Canvas. Coordinates are TOP-LEFT based in Miro px with the artifact's top-left at (0,0). Miro's API positions items by CENTRE: centre_x = x + w/2, centre_y = y + h/2. Place items verbatim — do not improvise geometry. Titles/tips must match templates/opportunity-canvas.md. Boxes are deliberately unnumbered (no prescribed order); the 'cell' field is an internal layout key only and must never appear on the board.

style.placement_note: Cell title sits inset ~30px from the cell's top-left; tip text directly beneath it, wrapped to ~60% of cell width. Everything else stays open space for the team's stickies (~80% of each cell).
style.builder_caution: Miro auto-scales a text item's WIDTH when its font size changes. Set size and width together at creation; if you resize text later, re-assert the width afterwards and re-verify nothing crosses a cell or frame edge.

cells.title: Why should the customer care? — Problems + desires = customer opportunity
cells.tip: Tip: start with what's motivating the customer. Then: what do they wish were true (the desire), and what gets in the way of getting it done (the problem)? Problem + desire = the opportunity. E.g. — I'm motivated to eat healthy. It's hard to figure out what's healthy (problem). I want something tasty (desire). Opportunity: help me find tasty food that's nutritionally simple to understand. A problem alone leads to a salad; the opportunity leads to a chocolate fudge protein shake. The customer hires what overlaps both.

cells.title: Empathy mapping
cells.tip: Tip: think through the what, why, when, where, how — and what they're feeling while doing, seeing, hearing — until you understand the customer's context (easy to go over the top). Then collaboratively list the gains (wants and needs — the measures of success) and pains (frustrations, anxieties, fears). Struggling with the opportunity box? Start here — this is never a sequential process :)

cells.title: User & customer cohorts
cells.tip: Tip: dealing with a multi-sided platform? Think through each side at a high level. Slice however it helps — channel, market, behaviour, attitude. No hard rules. You're designing for a specific cohort, even when the feature is exposed to everyone. Struggling? Map back to the opportunity box.

cells.title: Solutions today
cells.tip: Tip: how do they solve this today? Competitors, an operational process, or existing features on the current product — or they just live with it. What works well about today's way? You'll have to beat that, or keep it.

cells.title: Why the business should care
cells.tip: Tip: tie it to a number the business already tracks — retention, GMV, support costs, whatever fits. What does it cost us to do nothing? A rough back-of-envelope t-shirt sizing of reach and impact — or even a TAM — beats 'big opportunity'.

cells.title: How might we…?
cells.tip: Tip: turn what you learned across the canvas into 'How might we…' questions — note which box each maps back to.

ground_rules.heading: Ground rules
rules: Slot frameworks in and out freely — stack-rank on SWAGs? Cool. Quotes over JTBD? Happy days.
Time-box exceeded? Skip a step. Bias to action — analysis paralysis kills more opportunities than bad ranking does.
This is not a sequence — the boxes carry no numbers on purpose. Start anywhere, jump anywhere; no magic order of conversation produces a silver-bullet opportunity.
A tool, not gospel — depart from any box or template whenever your thinking argues better.
